blocks.text: Consider a RLC-series circuit having an alternating voltage source with variable frequency as shown in Fig.17.11(a). The impedance diagram of RLC-series circuit is shown in Fig.17.11(b) in which inductive reactance X_L = ω L and capacitive reactance X_C = 1 /ω C are directed opposite to each other.

blocks.alt: (a) R, L and C in series with an AC source, current I. Beside them three small graphs against time: for R, Vo and Io in step; for L, Io with Vo a quarter cycle ahead; for C, Io with Vo a quarter cycle behind. A rotating phasor circle shows XL at +90 degrees, XC at -90 degrees, 180 degrees apart. (b) Impedance triangle ABC: R along AB, XL - XC up BC, and Z along AC at angle theta.
blocks.caption: Figure 17.11 (a), (b): (a) RLC-series circuit with its AC source phasor diagram; (b) the impedance vector diagram of RLC-series circuit (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 17.11 (a), (b)).

blocks.text: The impedance of the RLC-series circuit is:
When frequency is high, then X_L = ωL is much greater than X_C = 1/ω C, and hence the inductance X_L dominates at high frequency, so RLC-series circuit behaves as RL-series circuit.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: X_L is the inductive reactance, not the inductance: at high frequency the inductive reactance X_L dominates.

When frequency is low, then X_C = 1 / ωC is much greater than X_L = ω L, and hence the capacitance X_C dominates at low frequency, hence RLC series circuit behaves as RC series circuit as shown in Fig.17.11(b).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: X_C is the capacitive reactance, not the capacitance: at low frequency the capacitive reactance X_C dominates.
In between these frequencies, there will be a frequency ωᵣ at which X_L = X_C. At this condition, RLC-series circuit behaves as pure resistive R-circuit as shown in Fig.17.11(c).

blocks.title: Brain teaser
blocks.text: Guess the name of the AC circuit used in the ceiling fan?

blocks.alt: Ceiling-fan wiring: the live wire passes through an ON/OFF switch; the top wire carries the running winding (stator) and returns down the right side to the neutral wire; a second branch carries the capacitor and the starting winding (stator) down to the neutral wire; the rotor is in the middle; an arrow marks the single phase supply.
blocks.caption: Brain teaser: wiring of a ceiling fan (original drawing after the textbook's picture).

blocks.text: This condition is called resonance. Thus, at resonance, the inductive reactance X_L being equal and opposite to capacitive reactance X_C, cancel each other. The value of resonance frequency fᵣ can be obtained by applying the condition:

blocks.alt: (c) A single horizontal arrow R: at XL = XC only the resistance remains. (d) Current I against frequency f: a sharp peak at the resonance frequency fr, with a dashed line at the peak, a double arrow from the axis to the peak and horizontal arrows on both sides of the curve.
blocks.caption: Figure 17.11 (c), (d): (c) Vector diagram showing that the RLC-series circuit behaves as a pure resistive R-circuit at XL = XC; (d) RLC-series circuit resonance at XL = XC (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 17.11 (c), (d)).
